headline: PSX snaps back +1.02% to 175,285.78 as the Hormuz toll climbdown and an oil pullback calm nerves — but the naval blockade itself isn't over.
summary: Stocks bounced back today, with the KSE-100 up 1.02% to close at 175,285.78 — clawing back some of Tuesday's brutal 3.56% drop. The relief came after Trump dropped his proposed 20% toll on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, and oil eased off its multi-week highs. At home, the picture stays solid: State Bank held rates at 11.5%, inflation eased to 11.1%, and reserves keep climbing. But the underlying US-Iran standoff and naval blockade are still live, so the desk isn't calling an all-clear — banks and fertilizer look better placed than energy-cost-sensitive names like OMCs and autos right now.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: High policy rate (SBP holding 11.5%) keeps carry income strong, and today's bounce was bank-led — UBL alone added 373 index points; several names (UBL, HBL, MCB, BAFL, NBP) screen 'attractive' on cheap valuations and covered double-digit dividend yields.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive with low direct oil-import exposure — macro's own sector tilt flags it as one of the better-insulated groups while the Hormuz situation stays unresolved.

sectors.name: E&P (Oil & Gas exploration)
sectors.why: Elevated crude (Brent still near $85) helps OGDC/PPL/MARI margins on paper, but the sector has been whipsawed hard this week by the same oil-price swings that are driving it — a two-edged trade right now.

sectors.name: OMCs & refiners
sectors.why: Weekly fuel repricing and circular-debt exposure make PSO/ATRL/NRL/PRL vulnerable if oil snaps back up before Friday's price review — the naval blockade resolution isn't confirmed yet.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported input costs and inflation-squeezed consumer demand are a macro headwind, even though a couple of individual names (HCAR, GAL) are showing isolated technical strength today — worth watching, not trusting as a sector call.

sectors.name: Textiles / exporters
sectors.why: Gulf freight-cost exposure stays elevated while the US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains formally in effect, even after the cargo-toll plan was scrapped.

watchlist.angle: A golden-cross (SMA50>SMA200) trend signal fired today per the desk's live scan — on HCAR's own history that setup has won 60% of the time over 10 trades, averaging +3.1% net per trade and still profitable out-of-sample. Results are due 2026-07-29, a real dated catalyst. But the fundamental read is a genuine caution flag: net margin is only 2.6% and the stock rates 'caution' overall — this is a technical-momentum name, not a value one right now.
watchlist.risk: Thin margins mean any slip in car sales, imported-parts costs, or fuel-linked freight hits earnings fast — a weak 2026-07-29 print could break the technical setup outright.

watchlist.angle: A 2-ATR-stretch-below-20MA mean-reversion setup triggered today — on NPL's own history it's hit 69% of the time over 13 trades (+1.2% net/trade), still working out-of-sample. The fundamentals back it up: a fair P/E of 7.36, a strong 43% net margin, and a well-covered ~24% payout ratio.
watchlist.risk: It's a short 7-session mean-reversion trade — it only works if this week's bounce holds; a fresh leg down (e.g. a Hormuz re-escalation) would stop it out quickly.

watchlist.angle: A trend + momentum combo setup triggered today (55% hit rate over 38 trades historically, +1.2% net/trade, still working out-of-sample). GAL was also just added to PSX's JS Momentum Factor Index reconstitution effective 2026-07-07 — a real, if modest, passive-flow tailwind. Valuation screens cheap (P/E 4.76, forward P/E 4.29) with a healthy 12.5% margin.
watchlist.risk: GAL sits in autos, a sector macro currently flags as 'avoid' on imported-input costs and soft demand — that headwind could cap the bounce even if the technical trigger works.

watchlist.angle: No live technical trigger today, but BAFL screens 'attractive' on fundamentals — a cheap P/E of 5.6, a well-covered 10.64% dividend yield (45% payout), and 16.6% net margin. Its Rs20bn Tier-2 capital raise was fully subscribed on 2026-07-10, strengthening the balance sheet, and results are due 2026-07-31, a real dated catalyst. On file, BAFL's golden-cross setup has a strong backtest (75% hit rate, +4.9% net/trade) though it isn't flashing today.
watchlist.risk: Banks are carrying today's rebound — a hawkish surprise at SBP's 2026-07-27 policy decision, or any Hormuz re-escalation, could reverse bank sentiment (and BAFL with it) quickly.

watchlist.angle: PSX's single largest index weight (8.63%) and a top point-contributor to today's bounce (+148.66 index points per Mettis Global). Fertilizer is one of the sectors macro currently favours. Fundamentals are a mixed-but-decent picture: improving forward P/E (6.79 vs trailing 9.08), a healthy 16.5% margin, and a 6.81% dividend yield. On file, FFC's 52-week-high-breakout setup has a strong backtest (78% hit rate, +3.17% net/trade) though it isn't triggering today. Results are due 2026-07-29.
watchlist.risk: It's a high-payout name (82%) — an earnings miss on 2026-07-29 could pressure both the dividend and the stock, and fertilizer margins stay exposed to gas-feedstock swings.

catalysts.event: Weekly petroleum price review (Friday) — watch for a further hike or a partial reversal given this week's oil pullback
SBP MPC — first monetary policy decision of FY27
PBS July 2026 CPI release — first print to capture this month's fuel-price moves and the Hormuz oil spike

risks: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports is still in effect — only the proposed 20% cargo toll was rescinded — so the Strait of Hormuz standoff isn't resolved; the desk's own conflict-stress gauge is still pinned at maximum (100/100).
Friday's weekly fuel price review (2026-07-17) could bring another hike if the recent oil pullback reverses, feeding back into inflation and pressuring OMC margins.
SBP's 2026-07-27 policy decision is the next real test — a hawkish surprise, if Hormuz-driven inflation risk resurfaces, would remove one of the market's current supports.
disclaimer: Research, not advice. The desk generates signals; it does not place orders. Losses are expected.
